key_risks.description: Leverage rose sharply after the $25.0B March 2026 senior notes issue, whose net proceeds funded an accelerated share repurchase, plus a $6.0B floating-rate term loan. Principal debt outstanding is $39.5B (vs $14.5B at January 31, 2026) against $11.4B of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Interest expense was $473M in the quarter vs $67M a year earlier, and $29.25B of principal falls due after fiscal 2030.
Under the accelerated share repurchase agreements, volatility in the stock price may obligate the company to deliver shares or make a cash payment to the counterparty on final settlement.

Significant other contractual commitments, including leases that have not yet commenced and commitments with infrastructure service providers, are not reflected on the condensed consolidated balance sheets.

The transition toward more complex pricing structures, including AI-driven consumption models, may make it harder to optimize pricing, predict attrition rates and accurately forecast revenue. Attrition may increase or fluctuate as customers reduce user counts.

Earnings quality: six-month net income of $5.6B includes $3.2B of non-cash gains on strategic investments, and Q2 income from operations was flat at $2,331M vs $2,332M. Six-month operating cash flow of $7.97B benefited from an $8.0B receivables inflow while unearned revenue fell $5.6B, so net income and cash flow overstate underlying run-rate momentum.

Professional services and other revenue fell 4% on weaker demand for larger multi-year transformation engagements, which the filing says may continue in the near term. The cost of professional services may also exceed related revenue in future periods.

Acquisition integration and financing: growth is aided by Informatica (closed November 2025). The filing says expense contributions from recent acquisitions are generally not separately identifiable, which limits visibility into organic growth and margins. Credit agreements entered into for Informatica add financing risk.

Tax exposure: prior-year returns are under examination in the United States, Germany, Israel, India and Australia. The provision for income taxes was $1,026M in the quarter vs $519M a year earlier, and an unfavorable resolution could require an adjustment to the provision.

bull_case: Revenue grew 11% to $11,345M in Q2 FY2027 (12% for six months), with Europe up 14%. Management raised the FY27 revenue guide to $46.1-$46.4B and guided Q3 to $11.42-$11.50B, ahead of the $11.41B consensus.

Data 360, Headless Platform, and Other grew 20% in the quarter and 22% for six months, and now makes up 33% of subscription and support revenue. This points to a growing data and context layer under Agentforce.

Backlog supports forward visibility: total RPO is up 11% year over year to $66.3B and current RPO is up 14% to $33.5B, ahead of revenue growth. The decline in RPO and unearned revenue since January is largely a seasonal billings effect.
Cash generation is strong: operating cash flow was $7,970M for six months against capex of only $316M, comfortably covering dividends of $729M.

Agentforce ARR has grown from $800M in February to $1.2B in May, up 205% year over year, and the Informatica deal adds data-layer capability. The consumption transition could raise long-run revenue per customer.
Six-month income from operations rose to $4.7B from $4.3B, the buyback has cut diluted shares to 821M from 962M, and quarterly GAAP EPS reached $4.29.
bear_case: Headline growth is flattered by Informatica (closed November 2025). The FY27 guide includes slightly above 3 pts of Informatica contribution, implying organic growth of about 8-9%, in line with the 8% growth in Agentforce Apps. Only $100M of the guidance raise is organic.

Reported net income of $3,526M is inflated by $2,613M of non-cash strategic-investment gains. Income from operations was flat at $2,331M with margin down to 21% from 23%, and six-month operating income growth of about 9% trails revenue growth of 12%.

Balance sheet leverage rose sharply: principal debt of $39.5B vs $14.5B in six months, a $6.0B floating-rate term loan, and quarterly interest expense of $473M vs $67M. Buybacks and dividends now depend on operating cash flow and refinancing access.

Operating cash flow was supported by an $8.0B receivables inflow, a timing effect, while unearned revenue fell $5.6B in six months vs $4.2B a year earlier. The extra decline suggests more than seasonality may be at work.

Agentforce is small, about 2-3% of revenue, and press-reported ARR figures conflict ($1.2B vs $1.5B). The filing says pricing was not a significant driver of revenue growth, and professional services fell 4% on weaker demand for large transformation projects.

Restructuring costs rose to $94M from $4M, and consumption-based pricing could make attrition and revenue harder to forecast. Off-balance-sheet infrastructure and lease commitments add to obligations.

what_to_watch.text:
**Organic Growth vs. Informatica:** Total revenue grew 11%, but Agentforce Apps grew only 8% ($7,193M vs $6,682M) while Data 360, Headless Platform, and Other grew 20% ($3,618M vs $3,008M) and includes Informatica. The FY27 guide includes slightly above 3 pts of Informatica contribution, implying organic growth of roughly 8-9%, and Data 360 supplied about $610M of the roughly $1,130M increase in subscription revenue. That said, organic growth of 8-9% is steady for a company this size, and management has said it expects organic acceleration in the second half.

-> Press management for an Informatica-excluded growth rate and for the organic growth of Data 360 as Informatica laps in November 2026.

**Agentforce Monetization and Backlog Quality:** Agentforce annualized revenue of $1.2B (up 205%) is only about 2-3% of a roughly $46B revenue base, press-reported ARR figures conflict ($1.2B vs $1.5B), and the filing says pricing was not a significant driver of growth. Total RPO of $66.3B is also below $72.4B at January 31 and below the $67.9B reported at the end of Q1. However, the January comparison reflects Salesforce's seasonal billing peak, and the like-for-like picture is better: total RPO is up 11% and current RPO up 14% year over year, ahead of revenue growth, while 205% ARR growth on a small base is an early-stage signal. Early consumption-model revenue should also look small at this stage.

-> Watch for an updated Agentforce ARR figure, a reconciliation of the RPO figures, and whether current RPO growth stays above revenue growth.

**Leverage and Capital Return:** The $25.0B March 2026 notes funded an accelerated share repurchase, lifting principal debt to $39.5B from $14.5B against $11.4B of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Six-month repurchases totaled $27.3B, $22.9B of authorization remains, and quarterly interest expense jumped to $473M from $67M. However, six-month operating cash flow of $7.97B and capex of just $316M leave ample room to cover dividends of $729M, and repurchases slowed to $84M in Q2 as the program shifted from the accelerated repurchase to ordinary buybacks.

-> Monitor interest expense, net debt, final settlement of the accelerated repurchase (shares or cash) and the pace of open-market buybacks against free cash flow.

**Earnings Quality and Cash Flow Durability:** Net income of $3,526M includes $2,613M of non-cash strategic-investment gains, and income from operations was flat at $2,331M with operating margin down to 21% from 23%. Six-month operating cash flow of $7,970M relied on an $8,035M receivables inflow while unearned revenue fell $5,576M vs $4,188M a year earlier. On the other hand, some of the unearned revenue decline is seasonal, capex is small, and free cash flow of roughly $7.65B for six months is real cash, and first-half operating income did rise to $4.7B from $4.3B.

-> Track non-GAAP operating margin, year-over-year unearned revenue and billings, and whether receivables collections normalize in the second half.

**Guidance Raise and Q3 Setup:** FY27 revenue guidance moved to $46.1-$46.4B from $45.9-$46.2B, and Q3 revenue is guided to $11.42-$11.50B against a $11.41B consensus. Of the raise, $100M is organic and $200M comes from the pending Contentful and Fin acquisitions, partly offset by a $100M FX headwind, so the quality of the raise is mixed. At roughly 0.4% at the midpoint, the Q3 guide is only slightly above consensus; that said, the raise came despite a stronger dollar, and RPO growth points to better visibility.

-> Monitor the Q3 revenue and cRPO results against the $11.42-$11.50B guide and the organic share of any further FY27 raise.

**Consumption Pricing and Professional Services Demand:** The filing warns that AI-driven consumption pricing may make it harder to optimize pricing, predict attrition and forecast revenue, and it provides no consumption revenue disclosure. Professional services and other revenue fell 4% to $525M on weaker demand for large multi-year transformation engagements, which may continue. On the other hand, a consumption model could raise long-run revenue per customer, and services softness may simply reflect a shift toward subscription-led deployments.

-> Watch for attrition commentary, any disclosure of consumption or Flex Credit revenue, and the professional services trend.

**Restructuring and Acquisition Amortization:** Restructuring charges rose to $94M from $4M in the quarter ($174M vs $40M for six months), and total operating expenses reached 56% of revenue vs 55%. Acquisition-related amortization in cost of revenues rose to $234M from $150M with Informatica. However, sales and marketing held at 34% of revenue and general and administrative fell to 6% from 7%, so cost discipline is partly offsetting these charges.

-> Monitor restructuring charges, the margin impact of acquisition amortization, and whether management quantifies Informatica's expense contribution.
